title: SITREP 5 — Operational Plan for Night Operations

fields.incidentName: Core Collapse — Mass Casualty Surge During a Network Outage
fields.summary: The hospital remains at Level 1 activation. Census stands at 349 patients, with the ED holding 52, ICU 3 North and 3 South at full capacity, and PACU overflow at three. The EHR remains read-only; registration and PACS remain down. The replacement core switch has arrived and will be installed at 21:30, with a target for full network restoration by 23:30. The Director of IT has confirmed that the interface engine ORRMC-INT01 remains stuck, and that the EHR cannot be used for new charting until the system is stable and reconciliation is complete. The CMO has approved the use of crisis standards of care for three expectant patients, who are now receiving comfort care with family. No new surge patients have arrived since 18:45, and all external transfers are on hold pending network stability.

actions.text: The Director of IT confirmed that ORRMC-INT01 remains stuck, and the EHR cannot be used for new charting due to risk of data split.
The CMO and CNO approved the continuation of crisis standards of care for three expectant patients.
The Planning Section issued a directive to suspend all new EHR charting until network stability and reconciliation are confirmed.
The Situation Unit compiled SITREP 5 for the AOC and unified command.

planned: The replacement core switch will be installed at 21:30.
The Director of IT will report network stability and interface engine status by 22:30.
The next SITREP will be issued at 22:30 or on significant change.
The CNO and CMIO will begin drafting the reconciliation plan for paper and EHR records once the EHR is stable.
issues: The EHR remains unusable for charting due to interface engine failure.
The risk of dual record entry persists due to patient identity conflicts.
Staff fatigue is increasing; 140 nurses have been on duty for 12+ hours.
No external communication has been issued to clarify the hospital’s status to the public.
The media continues to report on unconfirmed patient deaths and identity confusion.

instructorNote: This inject establishes the operational decision point for the night. The AOC must set the path forward: when to resume EHR charting, when to step down from Level 1, and how to manage reconciliation. Watch for whether the AOC defers to IT, or asserts command over operational decisions.
